text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - British stocks fell as a stronger-than-expected drop in unemployment revived inflation and interest-rate worries while the meeting of Federal Reserve policy-makers in the United States sidelined some investors. The FTSE 100 share index lost 7.4 points to 3,926.9.

FRANKFURT - The German DAX index of leading shares ended at a record high, continuing the rally started on Tuesday. The 30-share DAX index closed up 39.13 points at 2,773.43. In after-hours trading the DAX index stood at 2,770.61.

PARIS - French stocks closed weaker with a Wall Street dip at the open accentuating the consolidation after Tuesday's high for the year. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 11.94 points at 2,217.19.
ZURICH - Swiss stocks ended on a weaker note in slack trading as investors grew cautious given high prices. The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended down 1.75 points at 2,443.97.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks finished lower, battered by profit-taking as well as intermittent selling bouts of futures, with the market direction unclear and domestic investors quiet. The Nikkei 225 average had lost 226.99 points or 1.07 percent to 20,979.44.

HONG KONG - A surge in property stocks led Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index to a record close, with investors encouraged by the outlook for both interest rates and the property market. The index jumped 137.38 points to 12,943.69.

SYDNEY - Australian shares ended a subdued session slightly firmer, the continuing decline of News Corp. since its first quarter results on Tuesday holding back the market. The All Ordinaries index added 3.4 points to 2,346.9.

JOHANNESBURG - Caution was the watchword on the South African market, as shares clung to weaker levels after being knocked down by futures trading. The industrial index fell 16.1 points to 7,914.1, the overall index lost 7.3 points to 6,755.3, while the gold index added 10.3 points to 1,711.9.
